primary_secondary.note: Single-author literature review of AI pair programmer studies.

research_method.claude: Single-author literature review in four stages (Definition, Search, Selection, Analysis) following a prior review; Google Scholar search of selected SE/HCI venues plus iterative snowballing; thematic analysis with open coding; 23 publications; 11-category taxonomy and 12 open problems
research_method.nlm: Literature review / systematic survey with thematic analysis and open coding; 23 publications; 11-category, 53-subcategory taxonomy; 12 open problems
research_method.value: Single-author literature review in four stages (Definition, Search, Selection, Analysis); Google Scholar search of selected SE/HCI venues plus iterative snowballing; thematic analysis with open coding of 23 publications (20 papers, 3 surveys/blogs/articles); output is an 11-category, 53-subcategory taxonomy and 12 open problems
research_method.note: Search details (Google Scholar, snowballing) given only by Claude, not contradicted.

context.claude: Academic; review of studies on LLM-based AI pair programmers (Copilot, ChatGPT, Tabnine etc.), some with industry association; 23 publications
context.nlm: SE and HCI literature spanning industry, academic and OSS settings; 23 publications (20 papers, 3 surveys/blogs/articles)
context.value: academic (secondary/review); 23 publications (20 scholarly papers and 3 developer surveys/blogs/articles) on LLM-based AI pair programmers

dora_applied.note: Both state DORA is not mentioned.

space_applied.note: Both state SPACE is not mentioned.

ai_discussed.note: LLMs as AI pair programming assistants are the review topic.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not reported; NotebookLM only notes the taxonomy's team levels (up to multinational teams).

data_window.note: End year differs between extractors; no explicit coverage period in the method section.

cat_productivity.note: Productivity uplift, efficiency, time to completion/success synthesized as benefits and cognitive factors.

cat_quality.note: Quality of generated artifacts (no universal standard, 'gap in selected metrics'), non-compilable code, accuracy, complexity.

cat_collaboration.note: 'Level of Collaboration' taxonomy category is team size/setting and human-AI collaboration, not a collaboration metric.

cat_satisfaction.note: Agreed Yes but not confirmed in the full text: trust is a concern about AI tools and sentiment appears only as an open problem; no satisfaction or well-being measure is synthesized.

cat_activity.note: Borderline: code volume added/omitted appears once, as one cited study's productivity/quality measure [27]; both extractors class it as Productivity.

cat_devex.note: Cognitive load is a taxonomy factor, but the DevEx framework is not used (both say DevEx is not mentioned).

cat_agile.note: SDLC stages only; no agile/process metric.

cat_survey.note: NotebookLM lists usability perception/sentiment collected by questionnaires and interviews. Claude lists no perceptual metric, only the critique that large survey studies are self-reported; Stack Overflow Developer Survey is one source.

evidence.quote: To identify the potential and prevailing obstacles, we systematically reviewed contemporary scholarly publications, emphasizing the perspectives of software developers and usability concerns.
To conduct our literature review, we followed the process used in a previous literature review [34]. This procedure involves four distinct stages: Definition, Search, Selection, and Analysis.
The initial pool of collected papers served as a foundation for an iterative snowballing process to uncover further related publications within our domain of interest.
To achieve this, we used thematic analysis as our methodology.
Our investigative study encompassed a review of 23 distinct publications, inclusive of conference proceedings, journal articles, and developer surveys.
With LLMs increasingly serving as AI Pair Programming Assistants spurred the development of specialized models aimed at aiding software engineers.

4) Productivity: A significant uplift in overall productivity is confirmed by numerous studies [33], [40]. A particular investigation used the volume of code added and omitted as a measure of productivity and quality [27].
Efficient tools can potentially reduce the time span required to realize a task, encompassing the time to select, implement, and subsequently validate a solution against user specifications.
Diverse methodologies exist to assess various aspects of software quality. While a study reports favorable outcomes concerning quality enhancement [28], we perceive a gap in selected metrics.
